title: adm carrying AUCTION_PRICE, AUCTION_ID and CACHEBUSTER macros stays literal in preview
specRef: https://github.com/InteractiveAdvertisingBureau/openrtb2.x/blob/403cbba542de3a5d9cfcccd0a34e74b01b79a9f1/2.6.md#objectbid — win/loss macro substitution (${AUCTION_PRICE}, ${AUCTION_ID}) is only meaningful once a real auction has cleared; an inert preview must leave the tokens exactly as delivered rather than fabricate a resolution. GAM-style %%CACHEBUSTER%% is the equivalent non-OpenRTB spelling some adapters emit in adm.

response.value: MACRO TEST price=${AUCTION_PRICE} id=${AUCTION_ID} cb=%%CACHEBUSTER%%

specNotes: Core has no rule that inspects adm content for macro tokens; nurl/burl/lurl macro substitution (rules-response.js NOTICE_MACRO_RE) is unrelated to this field and is not exercised here — no macro-specific finding is expected from Core at any layer.
The literal "${AUCTION_PRICE}" text in the rendered body is itself proof the token was left unresolved, which is why it is used as the preview marker instead of a separate assertion.

public/ortbtools.app.js noteUnresolvedMacros() recognizes both the ${MACRO} and %%MACRO%% spellings and adds a below-frame note; that note is a real, already-shipped feature. It is not asserted here via expect.preview.limitation because tests/corpus/lib/browser.js measurePreview() computes limitationShown only from kind/refusal/CSP signals and does not read the notes strip — asserting it would test the harness, not the product.
